summary:
The Salado Shiner was a small freshwater fish that once moved through the cool, flowing waters of the Rio Salado, threading across the desert borderlands of Nuevo León and Coahuila in northeastern Mexico. Known from only four recorded locations, it lived within a narrow world — intimate, specific, irreplaceable.

By the late twentieth century, it was gone. Surveys in 1988, 1995, and beyond found nothing. No confirmed cause has ever been established; the exact forces that erased it remain unknown. What is known is that it will not return. The Salado Shiner exists now only in specimen records and memory — a quiet disappearance from a river that still flows on without it.
